## HIGH-priority finding details

### H-1: `dependencyTokenScope` field, `dependency-auth` step, and its API endpoint undocumented  (3/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx` lists every other `RepoMapping` field but not `dependencyTokenScope`; `customize/custom-steps.mdx`'s built-in step list jumps from `install-skills` straight to `install`; `reference/admin-ui.mdx`'s runner-callback endpoint table omits the dependency-token endpoint.
- **Source**: `src/config.ts:72-73` (`dependencyTokenScope: "installation" | null` on `RepoMapping`), wired through the New Project stepper and Edit dialog; `src/pipeline/steps/dependency-auth.ts` and `pipelines/autonomous.yml` (the pipeline step that fetches and installs the token); `src/index.ts:2877-2901` (`POST /api/runner/dependency-token`). Fully wired end-to-end with no mention anywhere in the docs.
- **Edit**: Added a `dependencyTokenScope` `<ParamField>` (with a `<Warning>` on the all-or-nothing scope and the publicly-reachable-orchestrator requirement) to `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx`; added a `dependency-auth` accordion to `customize/custom-steps.mdx`; added the `/api/runner/dependency-token` endpoint row to `reference/admin-ui.mdx`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs.

### H-2: "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" wrongly required  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `quickstart.mdx`, `setup/github-app.mdx`, and `setup/target-repo.mdx` each told the reader to enable this repo setting, warning that Claude cannot open PRs / the workflow will fail without it.
- **Source**: `src/pipeline/steps/push.ts:179-192,272-277` — the push step opens the PR using a GitHub App installation token via direct REST calls, not the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` this setting restricts; `workflows/claude-implement.yml:186-232` overrides `GITHUB_TOKEN` with the App's own token for the pipeline run.
- **Edit**: Removed the false requirement from all three pages; `setup/github-app.mdx`'s section was replaced with a `<Tip>` clarifying the setting is unnecessary.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs that surfaced it (2/3; not raised in run 3).

### H-3: Self-deploy (Deployments admin panel, `FLY_DEPLOY_TOKEN`) undocumented  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx` never mentioned "Deployments"; `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` had no entry for `FLY_DEPLOY_TOKEN` or the `AI_IMPLEMENT_SOURCE_*` build stamps.
- **Source**: `src/admin-ui/pages/deployments.ts` is a fully built panel (availability, last-deploy outcome, auto-deploy/announce policy, "Deploy now"); `src/admin-ui/sidebar.ts:25` gives it a sidebar slot; `src/admin.ts:235-266` backs it with `/api/deploy`, `/api/deployment-status`, `/api/deploy-policy`; `.env.example:179-203` documents the full feature including the silent-disable footgun when build stamps are omitted.
- **Edit**: Added a `### Deployments` section to `reference/admin-ui.mdx` (sidebar list, Platform group, three endpoint rows), and a "Self-deploy" accordion to `configuration/environment-variables.mdx`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in run 1; MEDIUM in run 2. Kept HIGH per no-downgrade rule.

### H-4: Dispatch breaker ("parked" issues) undocumented  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: No stable page mentioned "parked" issues, the dispatch breaker, or `DISPATCH_BREAKER_THRESHOLD`, despite the variable being canonical in `.env.example`.
- **Source**: `src/dispatch-breaker.ts` parks an issue+phase after consecutive dispatch failures; `src/index.ts:481` gates polling eligibility on `isParked`; `src/index.ts:708-734` posts a tracker comment naming the remediation; `src/admin-ui/pages/runners.ts:16-217` implements the "Parked issues" UI section; `.env.example:206-211` documents the threshold.
- **Edit**: Added a "Parked issues" subsection to `reference/admin-ui.mdx`'s Runners section plus two endpoint rows, and a "Dispatch breaker (parked issues)" accordion to `configuration/environment-variables.mdx`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in run 1; MEDIUM in run 2. Kept HIGH per no-downgrade rule.

### H-5: `reviewCheckNames` config key undocumented; default check-name list under-enumerated  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `customize/custom-steps.mdx` documented `reviewProviders` but not the separate `reviewCheckNames` key, and its parenthetical listed only 2 of the real 5 default check names.
- **Source**: `src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts:73` — `DEFAULT_REVIEW_CHECK_NAMES = ["review", "code-review-plugin", "claude-review", "claude code review", "claude-code-review"]`, plus a fuzzy fallback at `:394-401`; `reviewCheckNames` is read from `.ai-implement/config.yml` (`src/pipeline/steps/install.ts:16,74`) and, when set, replaces the defaults with an exact-match-only list.
- **Edit**: Corrected the `reviewProviders` description to point at the full default list, and added a `reviewCheckNames` `<ParamField>` documenting the defaults, the fuzzy-match fallback, and the exact-match override behavior.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in run 3; MEDIUM in run 2. Kept HIGH per no-downgrade rule.

### H-6: "Reports" admin panel entirely undocumented  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx`'s Work-group summary and Work section never mentioned "Reports"; no `/api/report` row.
- **Source**: `src/admin-ui/pages/reports.ts` is a fully built panel (fleet-by-repo table, one-shot/eventual/escape-rate KPIs, planning A/B comparison, runaways); `src/admin-ui/sidebar.ts:13`; `src/admin.ts:507-517` backs it with `/api/report`.
- **Edit**: Added a `### Reports` section under `## Work`, updated the sidebar summary, and added the `/api/report` endpoint row.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run to surface it).

### H-7: Orchestrator requires Node.js 24, not "20 or later"  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `setup/prerequisites.mdx` told readers to install "Node.js 20 or later," in two places.
- **Source**: `package.json:10-11` pins `"engines": {"node": ">=24 <25"}`; `.nvmrc`/`.tool-versions` pin `24.15.0`; both `dev` scripts run a Node-major check first that fails on an older major.
- **Edit**: Updated both mentions to Node.js 24, noting the startup check enforces it.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run to surface it).

### H-8: `.env` *is* auto-loaded by `npm run dev` / `dev:local`  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `setup/deploy.mdx` told readers `.env` "is not auto-loaded" and to manually export it or pass `--env-file`.
- **Source**: `package.json:18,20` — both scripts already run `tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env src/index.ts`.
- **Edit**: Replaced the incorrect Note with a one-line confirmation that both scripts load `.env` automatically.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run to surface it).

### H-9: Run caps and required Default Branch are already stable, not "new in latest"  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx` opened the Projects section with an Info box labeling the run-cap fields and required Default Branch field as "New in latest," directly above prose describing them as already live.
- **Source**: `src/config.ts:59-63` (`maxTurns`/`maxIterations`/`maxJobMinutes` on `RepoMapping`) and `src/admin.ts:1251` (`defaultBranch` required validation) are both present in this v1.1.0 checkout; `releases.mdx` already credits per-project run caps to the v1.0.0 release.
- **Edit**: Removed the stale Info box; the accurate description directly below it already stands on its own.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run to surface it).

### H-10: `gap_analysis_model` / haiku gap-analysis default is a removed, non-functional key  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `how-it-works.mdx`, `providers/anthropic.mdx`, `providers/aws-bedrock.mdx`, and `reference/gap-analysis.mdx` all claimed gap analysis defaults to a cheaper `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` model and is configurable via `gap_analysis_model:`. `customize/workflow-md.mdx` and `configuration/workflow-templates.mdx` documented the key as a working (or "reserved but parsed") option.
- **Source**: `src/__tests__/workflow-md.test.ts:49-56` proves the parser drops the key entirely and nothing consumes it; the seeded `workflows/WORKFLOW.md` no longer mentions it at all.
- **Edit**: Corrected all six pages describing the false haiku default/override and removed the two `gap_analysis_model` reference entries — gap analysis runs on the same model as the rest of the run in every case.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run to surface it).

### H-11: Fly machine memory documented as 256 MB, actually 512 MB  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `setup/prerequisites.mdx` and `setup/deploy.mdx` both stated the orchestrator "runs comfortably on a `shared-cpu-1x` machine with 256 MB of memory."
- **Source**: `fly.toml:18` provisions `memory = "512mb"`.
- **Edit**: Corrected both mentions to 512 MB.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run to surface it) — the exact resource figure an operator would use to size or budget a deployment.

### H-12: `/ai-implement` comment trigger now runs through the orchestrator's webhook, not `comment-trigger.yml`  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Nine pages described `comment-trigger.yml` as the file that handles `/ai-implement` PR comments, installed by every workflow sync, and stated or implied the GitHub webhook is optional because this trigger "never involves the orchestrator."
- **Source**: `src/workflow-sync.ts:14-32` — the current sync no longer adds `comment-trigger.yml` and actively removes it from repos that still have it; `src/webhook.ts:463-558` (`handleIssueCommentWebhook`) now parses `/ai-implement` comments itself; `src/index.ts:174-176,2955-2958` show the webhook endpoint is disabled entirely when `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset.
- **Edit**: Removed `comment-trigger.yml` from every "files this sync installs" list; replaced "the `comment-trigger.yml` workflow picks it up" language with "the orchestrator's GitHub webhook picks it up"; corrected the webhook-optionality framing in `setup/github-app.mdx` and `configuration/environment-variables.mdx`; added a dedicated section to `configuration/workflow-templates.mdx`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run to surface it).

## MEDIUM-priority finding details

### M-1: Skills marketplace catalog pins stable channel to `v1.0.0`, not the latest release  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `skills/installation.mdx` and `skills/releases.mdx` describe the stable channel as always resolving to "the most recent released version" (v1.4.0 per this run's pin).
- **Source**: `skills-source/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:13` still pins `"ref": "v1.0.0"` — the version before this repo's own versioned-installation feature shipped. No script in the checkout bumps this ref on release.

### M-2: Blocker-reasons table missing `file-overlap`  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/error-codes.mdx`'s "Blocker reasons" table lists only `concurrency`, `dedup`, and `no-mapping`.
- **Source**: `src/poll-selection.ts:11` types the reason as `"no-mapping" | "dedup" | "concurrency" | "file-overlap"`, and line 207 produces `file-overlap` when a feature-branch sibling's declared files overlap an in-flight sibling.

### M-3: MCP OAuth-proxy environment variables undocumented  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` has no section for the `/mcp` OAuth proxy, even though `setup/sso.mdx` already tells readers to register MCP callback URIs alongside admin sign-in ones.
- **Source**: `.env.example:139-164` — `KG_SIDECAR_URL`, `KG_SOURCE_REPO`, `MCP_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_ORIGINS`, `MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` are all real, documented-in-source variables with no counterpart on the env-vars reference page.

### M-4: Notifications page undercounts event kinds  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/notifications.mdx` states "AI-Implement notifies on two kinds of event" (run lifecycle, orchestrator lifecycle).
- **Source**: `src/notify.ts` exports five shape-specific functions; two are un-mentioned call sites with real operational value — `notifyStuckGiveUp` (`src/stuck-watchdog.ts:73`) and `notifyReaperBurst` (`src/reaper.ts:263`, fired when a sweep exceeds `REAPER_ALERT_THRESHOLD` destructions).

### M-5: Jira `profilesFieldOverride` / `AI-Implement Profiles` field undocumented  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx`'s Jira `ticketingConfig` reference lists `jql`, `repoFieldValue`, `statusFieldOverride`, and `repoFieldOverride`. `setup/target-repo.mdx`'s Jira custom-field walkthrough covers only `AI-Implement Status` and `AI-Implement Repo`.
- **Source**: `src/providers/jira.ts:203,235,302-312` — a third optional field, read from a multi-select custom field named `AI-Implement Profiles` (overridable via `ticketingConfig.profilesFieldOverride`), feeds `RunConfigV1.profiles` to the dispatch envelope. No built-in step consumes it, which is why this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

## Synthesis decisions log (audit-trail for reviewers)

### H-1
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH, Run 2 HIGH, Run 3 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** All three cite `RepoMapping.dependencyTokenScope` (`src/config.ts:72-73`) as undocumented in `team-repo-mappings.mdx`. Run 1 additionally flags the `dependency-auth` pipeline step missing from `custom-steps.mdx`, and Run 3 additionally flags the `/api/runner/dependency-token` endpoint missing from `admin-ui.mdx` — same underlying feature (Dependency Token Scope), so kept as one finding spanning all three docs surfaces rather than three separate findings.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 1 (`team-repo-mappings.mdx`, `custom-steps.mdx`), Run 3 (`admin-ui.mdx`)
- **Selection reasoning:** For `team-repo-mappings.mdx`, three candidates existed. Run 3's omitted the `default` prop entirely, violating `CLAUDE.md`'s rule that `<ParamField>` defaults belong in the `default` prop, not body prose. Between Run 1 (`default="off"`) and Run 2 (`default="unset"`), Run 1's label matches the admin UI's own default label ("off"), as recorded in the AI-Implement checkout's per-project settings table, and pairs the all-or-nothing security nuance with a `<Warning>` — consistent with `audit-reference.md`'s worked example for this exact field. Run 2's final paragraph also joins two distinct facts (all-or-nothing scope, orchestrator-reachability requirement) with "so," which reads as two beats in one paragraph. Run 1's `custom-steps.mdx` accordion and Run 3's `admin-ui.mdx` endpoint row had no competing candidates, so both were applied as-is.

**Edit candidates compared:**

Run 1's approach (selected) — `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx`:
```mdx
<ParamField body="dependencyTokenScope" type="string" default="off">
  Set to `installation` to let this project's dependency-install step read private sibling repositories — for example a private package registry or a monorepo split across repos.

  Leave it off and dependency install only sees this repository; a private sibling dependency fails to resolve.

  <Warning>
    The scope is all-or-nothing: the token can read every repository the GitHub App installation covers, not just a chosen subset. It also requires a publicly reachable orchestrator...
  </Warning>
</ParamField>
```

Run 2's approach (not selected) — combines two beats in the closing paragraph:
```mdx
<ParamField body="dependencyTokenScope" type="string" default="unset">
  Lets a run read private sibling repositories during dependency install...

  Leave it unset to keep dependency installs limited to the target repository, which is the default...

  Set it to `installation` to grant read access instead. The scope is all-or-nothing: it opens every repository the GitHub App installation can see, not a chosen subset, so it also needs a publicly reachable orchestrator...
</ParamField>
```

Run 3's approach (not selected) — missing the required `default` prop:
```mdx
<ParamField body="dependencyTokenScope" type="string">
  Grants the run's implementer read access to every repository the GitHub App installation can see...
</ParamField>
```

### H-2
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH, Run 2 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** Identical claim in both — the "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" toggle is not actually required, since every synced workflow authenticates PR creation with a GitHub App token. Same three docs files edited in both runs.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 1 for `setup/github-app.mdx`; Run 1 and Run 2 were byte-identical for `quickstart.mdx` and `setup/target-repo.mdx` (no selection needed there).
- **Selection reasoning:** For `setup/github-app.mdx`, Run 1 replaced the removed section with a reader-focused `<Tip>` explaining why the toggle is unnecessary — matching `CLAUDE.md`'s guidance that `<Tip>` fits a "you can skip the hard way" relief. Run 2 deleted the section outright with no replacement, leaving no answer for a reader who specifically came looking for this setting.

**Edit candidates compared** (`setup/github-app.mdx` only — the other two files were identical between runs):

Run 1's approach (selected):
```mdx
<Tip>
  You do not need to enable this repository setting for AI-Implement. Every synced workflow opens its pull request with the GitHub App's own installation token, not the workflow's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` that this setting restricts, so the toggle can stay at its default in every target repo.
</Tip>
```

Run 2's approach (not selected) — section deleted with no replacement, leaving the reader's question unanswered.
